questions.question: Which of the following describes the function of an enzyme known as dicer?

options.text: It degrades mRNA with no poly(A) tail
It trims small double-stranded RNAs into molecules that can block translation

suspectLines.text: 2. Stimulating CCR4/NOT complex-mediated poly(A) tail degradation
3. Inhibition of translation by targeting the 5′-methyl cap-binding translation factor

questions.explanation:
Dicer is an endonuclease that trims small double-stranded RNA into molecules that can block translation.

Dicer is an enzyme that cleaves the cytosolic dsRNA encoded by the genome and generates short, double-stranded (ds) miRNA. One of the two strands (the guide or antisense strand) is selected for loading into the RNA-induced silencing complex (RISC) which is composed of one of four argonaute proteins (Ago 1–4). The RNA then forms a mature, functional 21–22 nt single-stranded miRNA.

In the RISC complex, miRNAs can modulate mRNA function by one of three mechanisms:
1. Promoting mRNA degradation directly
2. Stimulating CCR4/NOT complex-mediated poly(A) tail degradation
3. Inhibition of translation by targeting the 5′-methyl cap-binding translation factor
